items.readable_text:
Content:
Let's determine how many cups are in [MATH: 96] fluid ounces.

Content:
We start with the unit conversion between fluid ounces and cups:

Content:
[MATH: 1\, \textrm{cup} =8\, \textrm{fluid ounces}]

Content:
Since we are converting from fluid ounces to cups, we divide both sides of the above equation by [MATH: 8] and obtain the following:

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{1}{8} \, \textrm{cups} = 1 \, \textrm{fluid ounce}]

Content:
The right-hand side reads [MATH: 1] fluid ounce, and we want to know how many cups are in [MATH: {\color{blue}{96}}] fluid ounces. So, we multiply both sides of the above equation by [MATH: {\color{blue}{96}}{:}]

Content:
[MATH: 96 × (1)/(8)cups|= 96 × 1fluid ounce; (96)/(8)cups|= 96fluid ounces; 12cups|= 96fluid ounces]

Content:
Therefore, [MATH: 96] fluid ounces equals [MATH: 12] cups.

items.readable_text:
Content:
For metric units of volume, there is one conversion we need to be aware of. That is

Content:
[MATH: 1 \,\textrm{L} = 1,000 \,\textrm{mL}.]

Content:
Let's use this to determine how many liters are in [MATH: 3,000] milliliters.

Content:
Since we are converting from milliliters to liters, we divide both sides of the above equation by [MATH: 1\,000] and obtain the following:

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{1}{1,000} \,\textrm{L} = 1 \,\textrm{mL}]

Content:
The right-hand side reads [MATH: 1\,\textrm{mL},] and we want to know how many liters are in [MATH: \color{blue}3\,000] milliliters. So, we multiply both sides of this equation by [MATH: {\color{blue}{3000}}.]

Content:
[MATH: 3000 × (1)/(1, 000)L|= 3000 × 1mL; (3, 000 ÷ 1, 000)L|= 3, 000mL; 3L|= 3, 000mL]

Content:
Therefore, [MATH: 3,000\,\textrm{mL}] equals [MATH: 3\,\textrm{L}.]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
In previous lessons, we explored converting larger units of volume to smaller ones. In this lesson, we will learn how to convert smaller units of volume to larger ones.

Content:
To convert between customary units of volume, we use the following unit conversions:

Content:
- [MATH: 1] gallon [MATH: =8] pints
- [MATH: 1] pint [MATH: =2] cups
- [MATH: 1] cup [MATH: =8] fluid ounces

Content:
We can visualize equivalent units of volume using measuring jugs filled with water.

Content:
For example, the two jugs below show the equivalence between [MATH: 1] gallon and [MATH: 8] pints.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/f930d4eba8c57a05b59bf92c02f4936f]

Content:
Let's get some practice at converting between different units of volume.

---

Item 2 — Tutorial: A Worked Example

Content:
Let's determine how many cups are in [MATH: 96] fluid ounces.

Content:
We start with the unit conversion between fluid ounces and cups:

Content:
[MATH: 1\, \textrm{cup} =8\, \textrm{fluid ounces}]

Content:
Since we are converting from fluid ounces to cups, we divide both sides of the above equation by [MATH: 8] and obtain the following:

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{1}{8} \, \textrm{cups} = 1 \, \textrm{fluid ounce}]

Content:
The right-hand side reads [MATH: 1] fluid ounce, and we want to know how many cups are in [MATH: {\color{blue}{96}}] fluid ounces. So, we multiply both sides of the above equation by [MATH: {\color{blue}{96}}{:}]

Content:
[MATH: 96 × (1)/(8)cups|= 96 × 1fluid ounce; (96)/(8)cups|= 96fluid ounces; 12cups|= 96fluid ounces]

Content:
Therefore, [MATH: 96] fluid ounces equals [MATH: 12] cups.

---

We want to figure out how many cups are in [MATH: 68] fluid ounces. So, we multiply both sides of the above equation by [MATH: 68{:}]
[MATH: 68 × (1)/(8)cups|= 68 × 1fluid ounce; (68)/(8)cups|= 68fluid ounces; (68 ÷ 4)/(8 ÷ 4)cups|= 68fluid ounces; (17)/(2)cups|= 68fluid ounces; 8(1)/(2)cups|= 68fluid ounces]

Therefore, [MATH: 68] fluid ounces equals [MATH: 8 \, \dfrac{1}{2}] cups.
